evidence: src/business/model/Order.ts: `@Entity('orders')` decorator on `export class Order` maps the domain class to the 'orders' database table (TypeORM persistence mapping, infrastructure responsibility).
src/business/model/Order.ts: constructor invariant, subtotal(), total() and cancel() are domain logic and belong to the business layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Order.ts is in the business layer, which is a domain layer. Most of the class is domain logic: the constructor checks that an order has at least one line, subtotal() and total() compute money values, and cancel() guards the status change. That all belongs here. The problem is the `@Entity('orders')` decorator on the class. It maps the domain model to the 'orders' database table through TypeORM, so the file also carries persistence work: object-relational mapping and table naming. That responsibility belongs to the persistence layer (infrastructure kind). Which way the typeorm import points is out of scope. The finding is about the decorator itself, which puts ORM storage metadata into the domain entity.

violations.message: The `@Entity('orders')` decorator on class Order maps the domain entity to the 'orders' database table with TypeORM. That is persistence/ORM work, which belongs to the persistence (infrastructure) layer, not the business (domain) layer.
